final_candidates.decision_summary: Abolishes the critical active-site arginine required for substrate binding and catalytic turnover, resulting in complete loss of function.
Introduces a rigid, helix-breaking proline at residue 222, disrupting local secondary structure and severely impairing enzymatic function.
Neutralizes the essential positive charge of the catalytic arginine at position 157, markedly impairing enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 loss-of-function candidates are clearly differentiated from the remaining pool with strong biochemical and pathogenicity support.

history.rationale: Arg157 is a critical catalytic residue that stabilizes the FAD cofactor; clinically documented substitution abolishes enzymatic activity causing severe homocystinuria.
Shows pathogenic classification (0.629) consistent with active-site impairment, though slightly less disruptive than R157A.
Alanine substitution at Arg157 eliminates the essential salt bridge to FAD, severely impairing cofactor binding and eliminating catalytic function.
AlphaMissense predicts high pathogenicity (0.973), confirming that disrupting the catalytic arginine abolishes MTHFR activity.
Pro39 is located in the conserved N-terminal catalytic domain entry loop; substitution to leucine causes severe loss of function in clinical deficiency.
Very low pathogenicity score (0.077) suggests this substitution is well tolerated and unlikely to cause LOF.
Thr34 is a conserved structural anchor in the catalytic domain; the clinical T34M substitution destabilizes the local fold and abolishes activity.
Predicted benign with a low score of 0.125, failing to support a robust loss-of-function effect.
Gly162 resides in the conserved cofactor-binding loop; introducing a bulky charged arginine creates steric clashes that disrupt active-site geometry.
AlphaMissense predicts a benign score of 0.262, downgrading confidence in severe loss-of-function.
Asp177 is an invariant acidic residue within the catalytic core; alanine substitution disrupts critical hydrogen bonding necessary for catalysis.
Obtained an ambiguous pathogenicity score (0.473), suggesting partial or context-dependent functional impairment.
Ala222 is part of a key alpha-helix; introduction of helix-breaking proline severely disrupts catalytic core architecture, eliminating residual activity.
AlphaMissense assigns a 0.953 pathogenicity score, indicating that proline insertion at this key structural position causes severe loss-of-function.
Glu232 is a conserved carboxylate in the active-site pocket involved in proton transfer/substrate positioning; alanine substitution ablates catalytic turnover.
Low AlphaMissense score (0.136) indicates high tolerance and low likelihood of abolishing activity.
Asp234 forms part of the conserved FEAD motif in the catalytic cleft; loss of the negative charge disrupts active-site electrostatic organization.
AlphaMissense score of 0.076 indicates minimal disruption, heavily contradicting the LOF objective.
Arg266 coordinates substrate and cofactor intermediates; glutamine substitution removes essential positive charge, causing severe loss of function.
AlphaMissense predicts a benign impact (0.109), weakening its candidacy for complete enzyme inactivation.
